h: Even at Sinai Torah Prepared for Human Vulnerability

p: Rather, just as with Shemittah... were stated, etc.,
so too all of them, etc."
it would not be so puzzling
what the mitzvah has to do with Mount Sinai.
And also the answer is not understood:
why did it choose specifically the mitzvah of Shemittah
to teach about the whole Torah,
that everything was stated at Sinai?
"General rules and details were stated at Sinai,
and stated a third time in the plains of Moav, etc."
so that Yisrael be a kingdom of Kohanim,
as they will be in the future,
"And you shall be called the Kohanim of Hashem":
that they be only servants of Hashem;
that the Angel of Death would not
as it was before the sin,
And afterward, in the Ohel Moed,
although it was already after the damage,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה חֵלֶק מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
it was still the portion of Moshe Rabbeinu:
only to those who ate the mann
(as they said in the Mechilta and Tanchuma),
and in this too there were levels
"for tzaddikim it fell at the doors of their homes;
for average people, they went out and gathered;
for the wicked, they roamed about and gathered";
וְאִם הָיָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And had Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
it would have remained so forever;
that it was no longer fit for this.
And afterward, in the plains of Moav,
which was the portion of Yehoshua,
then each one began to work:
this one turning to his field
and that one to his vineyard;
which is the beginning of Torah she'b'al peh,
"and Moshe said these of his own accord."
"a place where there is no forgetting."
had the First Tablets not been broken,
Torah would not have been forgotten from Yisrael."
which were given after the damage,
that guarding is needed lest one forget.
לֹא הָיָה אֶלָּא עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת לְבַד
there were only the Ten Commandments,
and in the Second Tablets I give you
there would have been given to them
only the five books of the Torah, etc."
and recognize that the land is Hashem's
have to do with Mount Sinai,
which was then in such a state
only for the service of Hashem Yisbarach,
and there was then no place
only in the plains of Moav,
And here it taught regarding this mitzvah
that it too was stated at Sinai:
that if their state would deteriorate
they would have Shemittah and Yovel.
And the pasuk comes to teach us
the matter of what they said (Avos 2:4):
That is: even one who has merited
לִהְיוֹת בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא אַף בְּחַיָּיו
to be a ben Olam HaBa even in his lifetime,
in this world a taste of the World to Come
the turmoil of the yetzer hara
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְצִיאַת רַע בָּעוֹלָם
as long as there is the existence of evil in the world.
That is: then at Mount Sinai,
like Adam HaRishon before the damage,
and nevertheless the serpent had the power
to enter him and entice him;
and who is greater for us than Yaakov Avinu,
who was like Adam HaRishon before the damage?
And he said, "What is lightest of the light, etc.,"
for he knew nothing at all of bodily pleasure,
And about this the Torah wrote,
to teach us that even though then
of the Angel of Death and of the yetzer hara,
and it was then as it will be in the future,
וְעָמְדוּ זָרִים וְרָעוּ צֹאנְכֶם (יְשַׁעְיָה סא, ה)
"And strangers shall stand and tend your flocks" (Yeshayahu 61:5),
and had the true rectification been,
there would have been no need at all for labor,
bring forth loaves of fine bread,
as it will in the future
nevertheless there was stated at Mount Sinai
for they might yet damage things,
the existence of evil among the nations,
and then they will need labor,
עַד שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁמוֹר שְׁמִיטָּה גַּם כֵּן
until he does not keep Shemittah either,
him to sell his movable goods,
and afterward his fields and his house,
even to a convert, to a gentile and to idolatry,
in the order of the sections,
as they said in the Gemara (Kiddushin 20a).
And from this it is learned
that the whole Torah was stated
their general rules and fine points — at Sinai:
שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְצִיאוּת מֵרַע בָּעוֹלָם
for as long as there is existence of evil in the world,
the 613 kinds of counsel are needed
to be saved from the accusation of the yetzer hara,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פב, ב)
וְזֶה עִנְיַן אַל תַּאֲמִין בְּעַצְמְךָ וְכוּלֵּי
And this is the matter of "Do not trust yourself, etc.":
that one not rely on his own stature
that he can guard himself from the yetzer hara;
and were it not for the help of the Holy One, blessed is He,
and "whoever is greater than his fellow,
his yetzer is greater than him"
and the mitzvah of Shemittah is needed,
which is like the holiness of Shabbos,

Remembering Torah and Guarding Against Forgetfulness
Shemittah Prepares for the Possibility of Decline
Every Level Still Needs Torah and Divine Help

paragraphs.text: Source: Berachos 35b — “… — מלאכתן נעשית על ידי אחרים, שנאמר: ״ועמדו זרים ורעו צאנכם וגו׳״, ובזמן שאין ישראל עושין רצונו של מקום — מלאכתן נעשית על ידי עצמן, שנאמר: ״ואספת דגנך״. ולא עוד …” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 102) — “Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says: Is it possible that a person plows in the plowing season and sows in the sowing season and harvests in the harvest season and threshes in the threshing season and winnows in the windy season, …”

paragraphs.text: Source: Kiddushin 82b — “… קוני. מה אלו שלא נבראו אלא לשמשני מתפרנסים שלא בצער, ואני שנבראתי לשמש את קוני – אינו דין שאתפרנס שלא בצער? אלא שהרעותי את מעשי וקיפחתי את פרנסתי, שנאמר: ״עונותיכם …” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 175) — “The mishna taught that Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: Have you ever seen a beast or a bird that has a trade? It is taught in the Tosefta (5:13): Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: I never saw a deer work …”

paragraphs.text: Source of the quoted words: Sukkah 52a — “אמר אביי: אי מאן דסני לי הוה, לא הוה מצי לאוקומי נפשיה. אזל תלא נפשיה בעיבורא דדשא ומצטער. אתא ההוא סבא, תנא ליה: כל הגדול מחבירו — יצרו גדול הימנו.” — “Abaye said: In that situation, if instead of that man it had been one whom I hate, a euphemism for himself, he would not have been able to restrain himself from sinning. After becoming aware of so great a shortcoming …”

rich.text: “אמר אביי: אי מאן דסני לי הוה, לא הוה מצי לאוקומי נפשיה. אזל תלא נפשיה בעיבורא דדשא ומצטער. אתא ההוא סבא, תנא ליה: כל הגדול מחבירו — יצרו גדול הימנו.”
